cards.title: Fund your first production run with crowdfunding plus community
cards.summary: Use Kickstarter-style pre-orders, Facebook groups, cross-promotions and local outreach to raise production capital when you cannot self-fund.
cards.use_when: Product launch funding when you have a prototype but not the cash for a factory minimum order.

cards.title: Audit your factory before paying for a production run
cards.summary: Verify that an Alibaba 'manufacturer' is a real factory with acceptable working conditions and quality before sending money overseas.
cards.use_when: Selecting and vetting a supplier for a first or large production order.

cards.title: Design and photography: buy premium assets instead of DIY
cards.summary: Listing photos and design drive conversion and differentiation, and DIY looks can read as inauthentic to shoppers.
cards.use_when: Creating or refreshing main image, gallery photos, A+ content or packaging for a listing.

cards.title: Launch with external traffic, then concentrate on reviews
cards.summary: Amazon is a search engine, so pair optimized listing assets with off-Amazon traffic and early review generation.
cards.use_when: Planning launch-week traffic and social proof for a new listing.

cards.title: Expect PPC to be the biggest swing factor in early margins
cards.summary: Early Amazon PPC can exceed product cost and push a growing store into losses, so plan spend, measure it, and be willing to get outside help.
cards.use_when: Setting monthly PPC budgets or diagnosing why a growing store is not yet profitable.

cards.title: Seasonality explains revenue swings before you 'fix' anything
cards.summary: A seasonal product will show sales and profit swings tied to its season, not only to your marketing quality.
cards.use_when: Interpreting a month-over-month revenue or profit drop before changing price, ads or product.

cards.title: UPCs, trademark and seller account: do the minimum viable setup
cards.summary: Cheap UPC codes work for a single product, self-filing a trademark is possible, and the professional seller account pays off above roughly 40 units/month.
cards.use_when: Setting up an Amazon seller account, listing a product, or deciding whether to upgrade your plan.

cards.title: Small tweaks to product and rating compound into organic lift
cards.summary: Continuous incremental improvements to the product and its rating can earn Amazon badges that drive organic sales.
cards.use_when: Managing an established listing and deciding where to spend improvement effort after launch.

cards.title: Do the due diligence you are tempted to skip
cards.summary: Rushing supplier and audience decisions costs more than the time saved, and the source's costliest mistakes were speed and research failures.
cards.use_when: Any point where you are about to commit money to a supplier, campaign or product without verifying assumptions.

cards.title: Pick a product you are genuinely interested in to sustain the work
cards.summary: Passion for the product supports persistence through supplier problems, PPC learning curves and slow months; a mismatch can lead to quitting.
cards.use_when: Choosing a product or category to build a brand around.

cards.title: Budget a first launch from real line items, not a headline number
cards.summary: First-launch cash needs range widely — one seller spent ~$9,600 before mistakes and another ~$26,500 total including freelancers.
cards.use_when: Planning how much capital to commit before launching a private-label product on Amazon.

cards.title: Delegating research and PPC can cost more than the tool
cards.summary: Hiring low-cost freelancers for keyword research, design or PPC without verifying results can waste the budget and bury mistakes.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to outsource keyword research, listing design or ad management.

cards.title: Take incremental action and a mentor rather than analysis paralysis
cards.summary: Committing to one method and getting guidance (mentor, peer group, or structured course) reduces expensive avoidable mistakes.
cards.use_when: Choosing whether to keep researching or start launching, and whether to pay for training or community.

cards.title: Amazon Individual vs Professional Selling Plan Decision
cards.summary: Choosing between Amazon's Individual ($0.99/unit) and Professional ($39.99/mo) plan determines Buy Box eligibility, ungating capability, and monthly cost structure.
cards.use_when: Deciding which Amazon selling plan to register for when opening a seller account, based on expected monthly volume and whether you need Buy Box or brand ungating.

cards.title: Brand and Category Ungating Process for Resellers
cards.summary: Amazon requires approval (ungating) per brand and category before you can list established-brand products, and denials are common so you must reapply repeatedly with invoices and photos.
cards.use_when: When you want to list a branded product on Amazon and are blocked by a gating restriction, or planning which categories/brands to pursue for reselling.

cards.title: Reseller Software Stack: SellerAmp, Keepa, SellerBoard
cards.summary: Three tools cover sourcing analysis, price/trend history, and reimbursement-plus-review automation for an Amazon reselling business, each with a different trigger point for adoption.
cards.use_when: Deciding which Amazon seller tools to buy and when, to avoid paying for software before you have listings or are already selling.

cards.title: Sourcing Method Choice: Retail vs Online Arbitrage
cards.summary: Retail arbitrage offers less competition and better in-store deals but isn't scalable, while online arbitrage is scalable at the cost of faster competition and price decay.
cards.use_when: Choosing how to source inventory for a reselling operation, or diagnosing why sourced products arrive already devalued and saturated.

cards.title: Reading FBA Inventory Breakdown: FC Transfer, FC Processing, Reserved
cards.summary: Use Seller Central's FBA inventory breakdown to diagnose where units are between shipment and sellable, and interpret FC transfer vs FC processing vs reserved states.
cards.use_when: When units you shipped to Amazon are not yet sellable and you need to know where they are, whether they're lost, or when to escalate for reimbursement.

cards.title: Prepping and Labeling Units for FBA Shipments
cards.summary: Remove original price tags and apply FNSKU labels over the UPC before shipping, so customers don't see your acquisition price and Amazon can scan your units.
cards.use_when: When prepping sourced inventory for an FBA shipment, especially clearance or discounted items that still carry store price stickers.

cards.title: Repricing Listings to Stay Competitive as the Market Moves
cards.summary: Ship-and-forget listings become unprofitable as prices shift, so reprice manually at first and move to repricing software past roughly 25 active listings.
cards.use_when: After units become active on Amazon, to keep prices competitive and protect margin against price drops, or when managing a growing listing count becomes too slow to check by hand.

cards.title: When and How to Outsource Sourcing and Prep
cards.summary: Outsource only after you master the business yourself, starting with sourcing via trained VAs and prep via a tax-free-state prep center.
cards.use_when: When an Amazon reselling operation is stable and you want to reduce time spent on the two most time-consuming tasks — sourcing and prepping — to scale.

cards.title: Creating the Amazon Seller Account: Required Documents and Setup
cards.summary: Assemble the required identity, payment, banking, and tax documents before signing up, and anticipate card-linking friction at registration.
cards.use_when: When registering an Amazon seller account and gathering the documents and payment methods needed to complete signup.

cards.title: Sequencing the Amazon Reseller Startup: Research to First Sales
cards.summary: A beginner reseller sequence — research, open account, buy supplies, get ungated, add software, source, prep and ship, track inventory, reprice — avoids paying for tools before they're useful.
cards.use_when: When planning the order of operations for launching an Amazon reselling business and deciding what to do (and spend on) at each stage.

cards.title: Four pillars of ecommerce security mapped to store controls
cards.summary: Frame storefront security work around privacy, integrity, authentication and non-repudiation, and translate each pillar into concrete store controls.
cards.use_when: Auditing or planning your store's security program and deciding which controls to add next across PDP, account, checkout and order records.

cards.title: Layered defense: block malicious traffic before it reaches origin
cards.summary: Combine a CDN and WAF in front of the origin, plus MFA on admin/account access, so no single control is the only barrier.
cards.use_when: Designing the network and access architecture of a self-hosted or heavily customized storefront that must absorb bots, DDoS and random malicious traffic.

cards.title: SSL/TLS: encrypt data in transit across every hop
cards.summary: Deploy TLS certificates so customer data is unreadable to intermediaries between buyer and server, and treat missing encryption as exposed credentials and card data.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing transport security for a storefront, checkout, account area or admin interface, especially after migrating hosts or adding a custom domain.

cards.title: PCI DSS scope: who owns what across hosted vs self-hosted
cards.summary: Treat PCI DSS as applying to any business handling card transactions, and decide card-data handling based on whether you are hosted, self-hosted or using redirect/iframe payments.
cards.use_when: Deciding your payment integration architecture, evaluating a hosted platform like Shopify, or assessing how much cardholder-data responsibility your team actually carries.

cards.title: Protect against counterfeit sites and brand abuse
cards.summary: Counterfeit lookalike sites and content tampering damage trust and valuation; use packaging authentication and monitoring to fight them.
cards.use_when: Planning brand-protection work for a store selling branded or high-demand physical goods that phishing and counterfeit sites might imitate.

cards.title: Handle the fraud, dispute and delivery moment of uncertainty
cards.summary: Online buyers face uncertainty at payment, dispute resolution and delivery, so make these stages transparent and accountable to reduce fraud exposure and abandonment.
cards.use_when: Reviewing checkout, post-purchase communication and dispute handling to reduce buyer uncertainty and the fraud that exploits it.

cards.title: Anti-malware scanning and scheduled detection for storefront files
cards.summary: Malware such as card skimmers, spam injectors and redirects hides in store files; use continuous scanning plus scheduled scans to detect and clean it.
cards.use_when: Operating a self-hosted or plugin-heavy store and needing a routine for detecting malicious code injected into the site.

cards.title: Defend against digital skimming and payment-page tampering
cards.summary: Card skimming (Magecart-style attacks) injects code into checkout to steal card data; protect by minimizing third-party scripts and monitoring checkout code.
cards.use_when: Managing checkout page scripts, tags and third-party apps, or investigating an incident where card data may have been captured from your site.

cards.title: Bot, spam and OWASP-class application defense with a WAF
cards.summary: A Web Application Firewall filters spam, bad bots and common web attacks like XSS and SQL injection before they reach your store application.
cards.use_when: Configuring application-layer protection for a storefront and deciding what the WAF should block versus allow.

cards.title: Layer passwords, PINs and magic links for buyer authentication
cards.summary: Verify buyers with login credentials, card PINs, magic links or email verification so accounts and orders belong to real identities.
cards.use_when: Designing customer account login, guest checkout verification, or account-recovery flows for the store.

cards.title: Non-repudiation: keep evidence that orders and consents happened
cards.summary: Digital signatures and retained records let neither buyer nor seller deny a transaction, which matters in ecommerce where no live video exists.
cards.use_when: Setting up order records, consent capture and chargeback evidence for the store, especially for high-value or subscription orders.

cards.title: Treat security failures as a survival risk, not an IT line item
cards.summary: Cybercrime causes financial, market-share and reputation losses, and the source reports most small stores that suffer attacks do not survive six months.
cards.use_when: Making the business case for security investment, or deciding how much budget and staffing to allocate to storefront protection.

cards.title: Harden store networks against worms, Trojans and destructive payloads
cards.summary: Malware delivered via worms, viruses and fake software can hijack systems, erase or block data, and propagate malicious links through your network.
cards.use_when: Establishing endpoint and store-adjacent device protection, especially for teams running order management, warehouse or admin workstations.

cards.title: Route traffic through selective-permeability firewalls
cards.summary: Firewalls regulate inbound and outbound store traffic with selective permeability, allowing only trusted traffic through.
cards.use_when: Choosing and configuring firewall or plugin protection for a self-hosted ecommerce site.

cards.title: Automate high-risk order handling on hosted platforms
cards.summary: Hosted platforms leave platform infrastructure to the provider but you still own order-risk decisions, so automate high-risk order review and actions.
cards.use_when: Operating on a hosted platform like Shopify and needing a repeatable process for suspicious orders, refunds or account changes.

cards.title: Map payment-fraud controls: verification checks at checkout
cards.summary: Address verification, card verification and 3D Secure shift some fraud risk decisions to the checkout step, alongside PCI compliance for card data.
cards.use_when: Choosing and configuring payment verification settings for checkout, or deciding how much friction to add to reduce card-not-present fraud.

cards.title: Defend against denial-of-service and keep the store selling
cards.summary: Hackers can prevent legitimate users from using the store, reducing functionality; DDoS filtering and preparedness keep orders flowing.
cards.use_when: Preparing for or responding to traffic floods, slow checkout, or downtime during a peak sales period.

cards.title: Integrity: keep customer data unaltered to preserve trust
cards.summary: Integrity means using customer information as given, without changing any part of it, because alterations erode buyer confidence.
cards.use_when: Reviewing how order, address and profile data is edited and stored across the store, especially where staff or integrations can modify customer records.

cards.title: Privacy: prevent unauthorized access to customer data
cards.summary: Privacy means no party other than the seller the customer chose should access their personal information and account details.
cards.use_when: Reviewing app permissions, data exports, staff access and vendor sharing for the store's customer database.

cards.title: Run a continuous security review across store surfaces
cards.summary: Security is ongoing, not a one-time setup; the source's closing recommendation is proactive, continuous protection across the website.
cards.use_when: Setting a recurring security cadence for the store rather than reacting only after an incident.

cards.title: Shared responsibility model: what the platform secures vs. what you secure
cards.summary: On hosted ecommerce platforms the platform owns infrastructure, checkout and server-side PCI, while the merchant owns credentials, app permissions and data handling.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest security effort for a store on a hosted platform (e.g., Shopify) versus a self-hosted cart, and scoping what your team is actually accountable for.

cards.title: CNP fraud and card testing: the mechanism to defend against
cards.summary: Card-not-present fraud uses stolen card data validated through small test transactions before larger fraudulent purchases.
cards.use_when: Designing checkout fraud controls, selecting a payment processor configuration, or investigating a spike in small declined/approved orders on your store.

cards.title: Chargeback thresholds: know your danger zone
cards.summary: Track disputes using the processor's actual definitions and thresholds instead of copying a fixed chargeback percentage.
cards.use_when: Monitoring order-risk and dispute metrics, setting an internal alert threshold, or deciding when to escalate fraud controls before processor action forces it.

cards.title: Dynamic 3D Secure and the liability shift
cards.summary: Dynamic 3D Secure adds step-up authentication on higher-risk transactions and can shift fraudulent chargeback liability from the store to the card issuer.
cards.use_when: Configuring checkout authentication to reduce fraudulent chargeback exposure without adding friction to every legitimate order.

cards.title: Automated order risk handling with workflow tools
cards.summary: Wire fraud-analysis risk ratings into automated workflows that auto-capture low-risk orders and queue high-risk ones for manual review.
cards.use_when: Setting up order review and capture automation so fraud decisions scale without a human watching every order.

cards.title: AVS, CVV and 3DS: keep the three verification tools distinct
cards.summary: AVS checks billing address, CVV checks for physical card presence, and 3DS adds step-up authentication on higher-risk transactions.
cards.use_when: Configuring fraud-prevention settings or explaining to your team which control addresses which fraud vector at checkout.

cards.title: Confirm merchant PCI scope with the acquirer and payment setup
cards.summary: Determine the store's actual payment-data responsibilities and validation route even on a hosted platform.
cards.use_when: Understanding your compliance obligations as a small store, or checking that store operations do not introduce non-compliant card-data handling.

cards.title: Payment gateway selection: what to verify before committing
cards.summary: When choosing a gateway, check processor-level PCI DSS certification, tokenization and 3DS 2.0 support.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a new payment gateway or reviewing whether an existing gateway meets your store's security requirements.

cards.title: Account takeover, credential stuffing and phishing defenses
cards.summary: Credential stuffing and phishing feed account takeover, which the source links to customer churn and reputational spread.
cards.use_when: Hardening customer accounts and admin access against takeover, or assessing the retention risk of an account-security incident.

cards.title: Auditing third-party apps and integrations
cards.summary: Every installed app can access order data, customer information or store settings depending on permissions — audit access regularly and remove unused apps.
cards.use_when: Reviewing app permissions before or after installing storefront, marketing, review or fulfillment apps, or cleaning up an accumulated app stack.

cards.title: Digital skimming (Magecart): why hosted checkout reduces exposure
cards.summary: Skimming malware injects malicious JavaScript into checkout pages to capture card data as customers type, and hosted platforms reduce this exposure because merchants cannot modify checkout code.
cards.use_when: Deciding between hosted and self-hosted checkout, or assessing skimming risk from custom checkout scripts and third-party front-end code.

cards.title: Bot attacks, API targeting and DDoS: what to watch
cards.summary: Bots run card testing, price scraping, fake account creation and inventory hoarding, and 44% of advanced bot traffic now targets API endpoints handling checkout, inventory and accounts.
cards.use_when: Investigating suspicious traffic patterns, inventory hoarding, fake account signups or site slowdowns that could be bot-driven.

cards.title: Security failures as retention and conversion risk
cards.summary: Account takeover and missing HTTPS drive measurable customer abandonment, and the source ties security to conversion and retention decisions.
cards.use_when: Making the business case for checkout security signals, privacy transparency, or remediating a security incident's customer-facing impact.

cards.title: Privacy policy, GDPR exposure and third-party audit signals
cards.summary: GDPR applies to EU/UK customers regardless of store location, with fines up to 4% of global annual revenue, and SOC audits act as third-party trust signals.
cards.use_when: Publishing or updating a privacy policy, supporting an EU/UK customer base, or evaluating what independent security assurance your platform provides.

cards.title: Guaranteed chargeback coverage programs: eligibility and limits
cards.summary: Shopify Protect (formerly Fraud Protect) covers chargebacks and dispute fees on eligible protected orders for eligible Shopify Payments users in the US.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether a guaranteed chargeback-coverage program applies to your store and how it changes your manual fraud-review workload.

cards.title: Preventing card data from leaking outside checkout
cards.summary: PCI compliance on a hosted platform is maintained by keeping card handling inside the compliant checkout and never storing card data in notes, emails or spreadsheets.
cards.use_when: Reviewing order-management, support and fulfillment workflows for card-data handling that could break compliance on an otherwise compliant platform.

cards.title: Prioritizing fraud controls when resources are limited
cards.summary: When a store cannot implement every control, sequence by direct financial exposure: enable account protection, then automated risk handling, then verification and coverage options.
cards.use_when: Building a fraud and security roadmap for a small store, deciding what to configure first, or allocating limited operational time to security work.

cards.title: Assessing platform-level security defaults before you rely on them
cards.summary: Hosted platforms supply PCI compliance, TLS/HTTPS and fraud scoring by default, but you should verify what each default actually covers for your store.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a hosting platform's security posture during store setup or migration, or documenting which security obligations remain with your team.

cards.title: Bot and fraud monitoring for inventory and high-demand drops
cards.summary: Bots create fake accounts and stockpile high-demand products before real shoppers can buy, so inventory protection is a bot-mitigation concern, not just a security one.
cards.use_when: Planning a limited-release, high-demand drop, or investigating inventory that sells out unusually fast with suspicious buyer accounts.

cards.title: Four Pillars of Ecommerce Security: Privacy, Integrity, Authentication, Non-Repudiation
cards.summary: Frame a storefront's security posture around four named pillars so controls map to distinct failure modes rather than a vague 'be secure' goal.
cards.use_when: Auditing overall storefront security coverage, or deciding which control category a proposed security project belongs to.

cards.title: Multilayer Security: CDN Plus MFA as Defense in Depth
cards.summary: Stack independent security layers (notably a machine-learning CDN and multifactor authentication) so compromising one control still leaves others to penetrate.
cards.use_when: Designing or reviewing storefront defense architecture, especially before high-traffic launches or sales events.

cards.title: Preventing E-Skimming at Checkout
cards.summary: Reduce digital skimming risk by keeping web servers patched, vetting ad server code, and updating third-party APIs — and know the shutdown response if skimming is detected.
cards.use_when: Hardening the checkout page and payment flow against payment-data theft, or responding to a suspected checkout compromise.

cards.title: Reducing XSS and SQL Injection Risk Through Untrusted-Data Discipline
cards.summary: Hinder XSS and SQLi by treating every data-table edit and API integration as untrusted and scanning for vulnerabilities before deployment.
cards.use_when: Reviewing custom storefront, theme, plugin, or API integration code for injection vulnerabilities.

cards.title: Defending the Storefront Against Pricing and Inventory Scraping Bots
cards.summary: Combat bots that scrape pricing and inventory or hoard popular items by combining reCAPTCHA, API checks, old-browser blocking, and alerting.
cards.use_when: Protecting product pages, pricing data, and limited-inventory drops from scraping and cart-hoarding bots.

cards.title: Brute Force Protection for Admin Console and Customer Accounts
cards.summary: Protect the storefront admin panel and loyalty accounts from automated password guessing with strong passwords, rotation, and access limits.
cards.use_when: Securing the admin console, staff logins, or customer loyalty accounts against credential-guessing attacks.

cards.title: Controlling Spam via Comment Cleanup, CAPTCHA, and Root-Cause Analysis
cards.summary: Reduce spam that injects malicious links through blog comments, social posts, or contact forms by combining CAPTCHA, pruning, and tracing its origin.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up spam on storefront blogs, comment sections, contact forms, or review channels that could carry malicious links.

cards.title: SSL Certificates: What They Do and Do Not Protect
cards.summary: Use SSL certificates to verify site identity and encrypt connections, while recognizing they do not substitute for checkout-specific skimming controls.
cards.use_when: Establishing or reviewing baseline transport security on a storefront, or explaining to stakeholders what SSL does and does not cover.

cards.title: Firewalls as Traffic Regulation for Anomaly Detection
cards.summary: Deploy firewall software or plugins to admit trusted traffic, block untrusted connections, and make anomalies easier to detect before they enter the network.
cards.use_when: Selecting or configuring perimeter controls for a self-hosted or platform storefront.

cards.title: Inventory of Common Storefront Threat Types and Their Countermeasures
cards.summary: Use a threat-to-countermeasure map covering phishing, malware/ransomware, SQLi, XSS, brute force, e-skimming, spam, bots, and Trojan horses to prioritize storefront defenses.
cards.use_when: Building or reviewing a storefront security threat model and assigning owners to each countermeasure.

cards.title: Separate malware detection from checkout fraud scoring
cards.summary: Use endpoint and site protection for malicious code, and payment/order risk tools for suspicious transactions.
cards.use_when: Reviewing order-review and fraud-screening controls for a storefront.

cards.title: Staff Security Training, Least Access, and Offboarding
cards.summary: Lower insider and account risk by training employees, limiting sensitive-data access, enforcing password updates, and revoking system access on departure.
cards.use_when: Setting internal security policy for store staff, admin users, and departing employees.

cards.title: Educating Customers on Password Hygiene and Phishing Risk
cards.summary: Reduce account-takeover exposure by requiring strong credentials and teaching customers that your store will never ask for personal information by email or text.
cards.use_when: Setting customer account and loyalty login policy, or writing security-related customer communications.

cards.title: Why Ecommerce Security Is a Business Priority, Not Just IT
cards.summary: Position storefront security as protecting reputation, customer trust, and the operational ability to deliver goods as promised.
cards.use_when: Justifying security investment to store owners or stakeholders, or prioritizing security work against growth initiatives.

cards.title: Least-privilege admin access for your store
cards.summary: Assign each Shopify admin exactly the permissions their role needs, profile it, and revoke unused access immediately.
cards.use_when: You are adding a team member, agency, or contractor to your Shopify admin and deciding what access to grant.

cards.title: Two-factor authentication across every admin account
cards.summary: Enforce 2FA on all store admin accounts to add a second verification layer beyond the password.
cards.use_when: You are setting up admin security for staff, agencies, or yourself and deciding authentication requirements.

cards.title: Use unique admin credentials, MFA and compromise-driven password changes
cards.summary: Reduce store account takeover with unique credentials, stronger authentication and prompt revocation.
cards.use_when: You are writing the operating rules for who can log into your Shopify admin and how credentials are managed.

cards.title: Restrict and monitor admin panel login locations
cards.summary: Use IP whitelisting, geographic/time limits and login monitoring to constrain who can reach the admin panel and from where.
cards.use_when: You are hardening backend admin access against account takeover or rogue logins from unfamiliar locations.
